metaDescription: Five 4-1/2 inch angle grinders at or under $100, corded Bosch and DEWALT plus brushless cordless models, compared on amps, guard design and safety features.
expertTake: The Bosch GWS10-450P is the pick for most shops because a 10 amp motor, 11,000 RPM and a multi-grip paddle switch combine power with a slim, comfortable body. The DEWALT DWE4011 is the value pick for people who want a tool-free guard on a proven 7 amp grinder. Skip a cordless grinder if you grind for more than a few minutes at a time, because even the best 20V battery drains fast under a loaded grinding wheel. The extra budget over a basic grinder mostly buys a safer switch, a better guard and a smoother grip.
introParagraphs: An angle grinder spins an abrasive disc at 8,000 to 11,000 RPM, which makes it the fastest way to cut metal, remove rust and shape stone, and also one of the most dangerous hand tools in a garage. The features that matter are less about power than about the guard, the switch and what happens if the disc binds.

This guide explains what a modest budget buys in an angle grinder, how amps, RPM and switch style change control, and why wheel rating and guard position matter as much as the tool. The picks are listed above, with the reviews below. Listing prices move, and the cap reflects prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: BOSCH GWS10-450P 4-1/2 Inch 10 Amp Paddle Switch Angle Grinder
products.description:
A paddle switch is a lever along the handle that you squeeze to run the tool and release to stop it, so the grinder shuts off the instant your hand lets go. That is a safety feature as much as an ergonomic one, because a grinder with a slide switch can keep spinning if it falls from your grip. This Bosch pairs the paddle with a 10 amp motor spinning at up to 11,000 RPM and a narrow grip zone that fits smaller hands.

Compared with the DEWALT DWE4011 at 7 amps, the Bosch has a stronger motor and a more flexible grip, but the DEWALT has a tool-free guard. Versus the Bosch GWS8-45 at 7.5 amps, the GWS10-450P has about a third more motor capacity, which shows when you cut thick steel or run a cup wheel. For fabrication, rust removal and cutting rebar, it is the grinder to buy.

Ownership: use a wheel rated at or above 11,000 RPM, since a disc rated lower can fly apart. Keep the guard in place and the side handle tight, and let the disc reach full speed before touching the work. Replace the brushes when the tool sparks excessively, and keep the vents clear of grinding dust.
products.bestFor: Fabricators and DIYers who cut and grind steel regularly and want a paddle switch safety.
pros: 10 amp motor handles thick steel and cup wheels
Paddle switch shuts the tool off when released
Slim grip fits smaller hands comfortably
Lighter body reduces fatigue on long jobs
cons: Guard needs a tool to adjust
Corded design limits use away from outlets
Highest relative price among the corded picks

products.name: DEWALT DWE4011 4-1/2 Inch 7 Amp Angle Grinder with One-Touch Guard
products.description:
A One-Touch guard can be rotated without a tool, so you set it to deflect sparks away from your body in a second instead of hunting for a screwdriver. That matters because a guard left in the wrong position is a common cause of injury. The 7 amp motor spins at 12,000 RPM, which is the fastest no-load speed of the corded grinders here, and it is designed for faster material removal with higher overload protection.

The tradeoff is power. At 7 amps, the DEWALT has about 30 percent less motor capacity than the Bosch GWS10-450P, so it bogs sooner on thick steel and when using a cup wheel. A hex wrench in place of a spanner wrench makes wheel changes easier, because hex keys are in most toolboxes. For general metal cutting and light grinding, it is a dependable tool.

Ownership: check that the wheel is rated for at least 12,000 RPM, since that is the tool's speed. Replace brushes at the first sign of power loss, and keep the guard adjusted. Store it with the cord loosely coiled.
products.bestFor: Homeowners and trades who change guard positions often and want a proven brand.
pros: One-Touch guard adjusts without tools
12,000 RPM is the fastest corded no-load speed here
Hex wrench is easier to find than a spanner
AC/DC motor with overload protection
cons: 7 amps has less headroom than the 10 amp Bosch
Slide switch keeps spinning if dropped
Higher relative price than the budget picks

products.name: Bosch GWS8-45 4-1/2 Inch 7.5 Amp Slim-Grip Angle Grinder
products.description:
A slim grip is a body whose circumference is small enough for the hand to wrap around, which matters because grip strength fades fast when you hold a vibrating tool. This Bosch pairs it with a 7.5 amp motor delivering 11,000 RPM and carbon brushes described as durable for extended tool life. It is a professional tool aimed at repeated daily use.

Compared with the Bosch GWS10-450P, it offers less power and no paddle switch. Compared with the DEWALT DWE4011 it has a slightly stronger motor but no tool-free guard. For a hobbyist who grinds rust and cuts bolts, it is a sensible choice that will last for years.

Ownership: check the brushes after heavy use, and replace them before they wear to the spring. Use proper wheels, keep the guard on and avoid side-loading cutting discs. Wipe grinding dust from the vents, since steel dust is conductive and can short the motor.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who grind rust and cut bolts and want a comfortable, durable professional grinder.
pros: Slim grip fits the hand and reduces fatigue
7.5 amp motor delivers 11,000 RPM
Durable carbon brushes extend tool life
Professional build quality at a modest tier
cons: No paddle switch or tool-free guard
Less power than the 10 amp Bosch

products.name: ALLOYMAN 20V Brushless Cordless 4-1/2 Inch Angle Grinder, 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
A gyroscope chip monitors the tool's motion and cuts power when it detects a sudden drop or violent shake, which is the response you want when a disc binds and the grinder kicks. Three speeds, 4,500, 6,500 and 9,500 RPM, let you match the speed to the work: low for polishing, mid for general grinding and high for cutting. A brushless motor runs cooler and wastes less battery.

The tradeoff is endurance and speed. At 9,500 RPM the top speed is below the corded 11,000 to 12,000 RPM, so cutting is slower. Compared with the DCA cordless below, the ALLOYMAN includes two batteries and a safety sensor. Compared with corded grinders, it gives up sustained power but removes the cord from sparks and ladders.

Ownership: two 4.0Ah batteries cover a typical metalworking session, but a heavy grinding job drains one in minutes. Keep batteries away from sparks and hot metal, since grinding sparks can melt pack casings. Use wheels rated at or above 9,500 RPM, and keep the guard on.
products.bestFor: Users who value a kickback sensor and cordless freedom for light cutting and polishing.
pros: Gyroscope cuts power during kickback or a violent shake
Three speeds suit polishing, grinding and cutting
Brushless motor extends runtime
Two 4.0Ah batteries included
cons: 9,500 RPM top speed cuts slower than corded grinders
Battery drains quickly under heavy grinding

products.name: DCA 20V Brushless Cordless 4-1/2 Inch Angle Grinder, 8,500 RPM, 4.0Ah
products.description:
A tool-free guard rotates to any angle without a wrench, and a brushless motor delivers 8,500 RPM from a 20V pack. The 4.0Ah battery fully charges in about two hours, which fits a typical lunch break. It is a straightforward cordless grinder for jobs where a cord would be in the way.

The tradeoff is power and safety features. Compared with the ALLOYMAN, it has no gyroscope shutoff and only one battery. Compared with the corded Bosch GWS10-450P, it is slower at 8,500 versus 11,000 RPM and drains faster under load. For cutting a bolt, trimming a fence post or removing rust from a gate, it is convenient.

Ownership: carry a spare battery for long jobs, and use wheels rated for 8,500 RPM or higher. Keep the tool away from damp surfaces, and charge before the job. Check the guard after every wheel change, because a loose guard is a hazard.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who cut bolts, trim fence posts and need a cordless grinder for occasional jobs.
pros: Tool-free guard adjusts in a second
Brushless motor reaches 8,500 RPM
4.0Ah battery charges in about two hours
Cordless reach for fences and gates
cons: One battery means downtime on long jobs

buyingCriteria.explanation: Amps decide how well the motor holds speed under load. The Bosch GWS10-450P has 10 amps, the GWS8-45 has 7.5 and the DEWALT 7. A grinder that bogs on thick steel overheats and wears out. For daily cutting, choose 7 amps or more. A grinder that is too weak for a cutting disc makes the work take twice as long and generates more heat in the disc, which makes it wear faster and increases the risk of a break.

A paddle switch stops the tool when released, and a slide switch locks on. The Bosch GWS10-450P uses a paddle. A slide switch can keep the grinder spinning if dropped, which is the greater danger. A paddle also allows more grip options. Test the switch before every job by holding the tool away from your body and starting it, so you know how it behaves in a startled grip.

A guard deflects sparks and fragments if a disc breaks. The DEWALT and DCA have tool-free guards. Always use a wheel rated at or above the tool's RPM, since a 4,500 RPM wheel on an 11,000 RPM tool can burst. Check the date stamp on every wheel, since bonded abrasive wheels age and should be replaced after a few years even if unused.

Kickback happens when a disc binds, and the tool jumps toward you. The ALLOYMAN's gyroscope cuts power when it senses sudden motion. Corded grinders rely on technique and a side handle. Brace your stance so that if the tool kicks, it travels away from your body and not toward your legs.

Cordless grinders like the ALLOYMAN and DCA run at 8,500 to 9,500 RPM, below the corded 11,000 to 12,000. Batteries drain under load. Choose cordless for convenience and corded for sustained work. Spark-heavy work near a battery pack deserves a shield, a sheet of metal or a welding blanket in between.

A slim grip reduces fatigue, and a lighter tool is easier to control. The Bosch grinders have slim bodies. Vibration numbs the hand over time. Wear gloves, safety glasses, a face shield and hearing protection for any grinding job.

specDecoder.meaning: RPM is the disc speed with nothing cutting. It sets the maximum wheel rating needed.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT's 12,000 RPM needs a wheel rated at or above 12,000. Check the wheel's maximum RPM stamp, which must be higher than the tool's no-load speed.

specDecoder.meaning: Amps measure the motor's electrical draw. A higher amp motor holds speed under load.
specDecoder.watchFor: Cordless grinders do not list amps, so compare battery and RPM instead. A corded grinder's amps include startup surge, so a long thin extension cord can trip the breaker.

specDecoder.meaning: Disc size is the wheel diameter. 4-1/2 inch is the most common size.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not fit a larger wheel than the guard allows. A cutting disc and a grinding disc are not interchangeable, even at the same diameter.

specDecoder.meaning: A paddle stops when released, and a slide stays on until pushed off.
specDecoder.watchFor: A slide switch is more dangerous if the tool is dropped. A paddle switch is only safe if it is not taped or tied down.

specDecoder.meaning: Brushless motors use electronics instead of brushes. They run cooler and last longer.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not assume a corded grinder is brushless. Brushless cordless grinders often share batteries with other tools from the same brand.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at paddle switches, guards and kickback sensors. The Bosch GWS10-450P has a paddle and the ALLOYMAN has a gyroscope. We treated a paddle switch and a kickback sensor as the most relevant safety upgrades at this tier.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared amps and RPM, from the 10 amp Bosch to the cordless 8,500 RPM DCA. We compared RPM and amps while also noting that wheels must match the tool.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ergonomics
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored slim grips and light weight. Vibration and grip size matter more than they seem after an hour of work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Corded and cordless
howWeEvaluated.description: We split cordless from corded, noting battery drain under load. Cordless was judged on short, intermittent jobs, since heavy grinding drains packs quickly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Relative value
howWeEvaluated.description: We used price tier to compare what extra spending buys. We used relative price only and never quoted a listing price.

howToChoose.intro: Choose by what you cut most often, then check the wheel rating and the guard, since the tool is only as safe as the disc and guard on it.
Relative tiers only: spending more at this level mostly buys a stronger motor, a safer switch and a more comfortable grip, not a different kind of tool.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: Runs at 11,000 to 12,000 RPM with steady power. The Bosch grinders and DEWALT fall here.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: No cord, but 8,500 to 9,500 RPM and limited runtime. The ALLOYMAN and DCA fall here.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded for sustained work and cordless for short jobs.
No guard, switch or sensor replaces good technique: stand to the side of the disc, brace the tool and let the wheel do the cutting.

howToChoose.subheading: For Cutting Rebar and Bolts Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Cutting needs high RPM, a thin cutting disc and a correct guard. Use a rated wheel and clamp the work. Keep the cut line short and clamp the work so the disc does not pinch.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Bosch GWS10-450P cuts fastest. The DEWALT DWE4011 offers a tool-free guard. Cordless models suit short cuts.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You grind daily or need brushless corded power. The Bosch GWS10-450P shows where durability begins. Also budget for good wheels, a face shield and gloves, which matter more than the tool tier.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut a few bolts a year. The DCA cordless covers that.

maintenance.task: Inspect the wheel before each use
maintenance.why: A cracked wheel can burst. Ring-test and inspect it. Hold the wheel by the arbor and tap it; a clear ring means it is sound.
A loose guard offers no protection. Tighten the clamp. Never use a grinder with a cracked guard.
Metal dust blocks cooling. Blow it out with compressed air. Wear a dust mask when blowing vents.
Worn brushes lose power. Replace them in pairs. Replace both brushes together.
Sparks melt pack casings. Keep batteries clear. Never charge a battery that has been in sparks.

faq.q: Is a cordless grinder good enough?
faq.a: For short jobs, yes. For sustained cutting, corded is better. Choose by duty. A corded grinder remains the standard for cutting and long grinding.

It buys a decent corded grinder or a cordless brushless model. Listing prices move, so check the live cost. Budget for good discs and a face shield as well. Many buyers spend more on wheels than they expected, because a quality disc cuts faster and lasts longer.
With care, many years. Brushes and bearings wear first. Replace worn wheels and keep the vents clear. A grinder that smells hot or smokes during normal use should be inspected before the next job.
Use a wheel rated at or above the tool's RPM. Cutting discs cut, grinding wheels grind. Never use a wheel with a lower RPM rating than the tool.

faq.q: Is it safe to remove the guard?
faq.a: No. Never remove the guard. It protects from flying fragments. A tool without a guard is also not covered by most warranties.

faq.q: Do I need a side handle?
faq.a: Yes. Always use the side handle for control. Hold the tool with both hands.
